candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent (pre-Inside-Airbnb) Python/PostgreSQL survey scraper that collected Airbnb listing snapshots 2014-2017 across dozens of cities worldwide (schema: room, survey, search_area, neighborhoods, zipcode tables). The code itself has no data committed, but the author's site (tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data) hosts the bulk historical survey extracts as downloadable files (CSV/SQL dumps) for many cities/dates spanning 2014-2017 — older than anything Inside Airbnb's own CDN retains and predating our 13-city panel's Dec-2022 start.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived STR dumps pre-2023) with a source 5-8+ years older than our current earliest coverage; also a second, independent scrape methodology (not Inside Airbnb's own tool) so could crosscheck listing-count/price levels for 2015-2017 in cities we still care about (e.g. NYC, LA, Paris, London, Barcelona).
candidates.last_activity: archived/no longer maintained per author (author announcement 2017; repo still on GitHub)
candidates.geography: dozens of global cities (bounding-box + city surveys)
candidates.size_hint: code repo is small; bulk data lives externally on tomslee.net, size unknown, described as 'get the data' bulk downloads

candidates.name: Zhitaow/Airbnb-Data-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Inside Airbnb extracts for Seattle and Boston, 2015-2016: listings.csv, calendar.csv, reviews.csv for each city (row counts not stated in README, but calendar.csv implies day-level availability/price panels).
candidates.why_useful: Two additional cities (Seattle, Boston) not in our 13-city panel, with calendar-level (daily price/availability) data from 2015-2016 — genuinely older than our Dec-2022 start and includes a price-bearing calendar file, which is exactly the kind of pre-2023 vintage flagged as high value.

candidates.name: JoeyDeJager/inside-airbnb-data
candidates.what_it_holds: CC0-licensed repo (created Jan 2015) with a 'new-york-city' data directory; root has only LICENSE + README so the actual CSVs sit inside that subfolder (not enumerated here — a directory listing of new-york-city/ would confirm file names/sizes). Given the creation date, likely holds a very early (2014-2015 era) NYC Inside Airbnb snapshot.
candidates.why_useful: If the new-york-city folder holds an actual 2014-2015 listings/calendar dump, it would be one of the oldest NYC vintages available anywhere on GitHub, directly relevant to gap #1's NYC pre-Local-Law-18 hole (though this predates even that window).
candidates.time_coverage: circa 2014-2015 (unconfirmed, needs directory listing to verify)
candidates.size_hint: small, single city, contents not fully verified

candidates.name: junheecho/crawl-inside-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Small script to download all files listed on insideairbnb.com/get-the-data.html (i.e., automates a full bulk pull of every city/vintage currently exposed on the Inside Airbnb CDN in one run).
candidates.why_useful: Not new data, but a ready one-command method to snapshot the entire current Inside Airbnb catalogue at once (all cities, not just our 13); useful for scheduling a fuller point-in-time capture going forward, and to check for markets/vintages we don't currently pull.
candidates.time_coverage: current CDN snapshot only, not historical
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our own Inside Airbnb pull tooling; only useful if it broadens city coverage beyond our 13-city/120-market panel

candidates.name: YassineEng/Web-scraping-and-dataset-download-Inside-Airbnb

candidates.why_useful: Possible alternate acquisition path for Inside Airbnb data; marginal since it likely just re-pulls current CDN files like our own pipeline.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: likely duplicates our existing Inside Airbnb capture pipeline

candidates.why_useful: Could be repurposed as our own DuckDB/Parquet ingestion layer for Inside Airbnb pulls (we already query raw stores via DuckDB per CLAUDE.md), marginal net-new data value.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our own Inside Airbnb capture/query tooling

candidates.name: luminati-io/Airbnb-dataset-samples
candidates.what_it_holds: A sample of ~1000+ current Airbnb listings extracted via the Bright Data (formerly Luminati) scraping API, provided as a marketing sample for the commercial scraping service.
candidates.why_useful: Not historical, small sample, and points at a paid commercial scraping API rather than free/committed bulk data; flagged only because it demonstrates a live commercial Airbnb-listings API exists (out of scope per CLAUDE.md's 'no scraping airbnb.com beyond sanctioned sources' rule, and this is a vendor sample, not usable directly), so treat as informational only, not actionable.

notes: Hard 6-call gh CLI budget was hit fast because `gh search repos` free-text matching on generic Airbnb terms returns almost entirely single-city student/tutorial notebooks and Airbnb-clone web-app projects (excluded per instructions) rather than historical data mirrors; one call (get-the-data) hit a 403 rate limit and was not retried (switched to WebSearch/WebFetch instead of a second gh call, per budget discipline). Genuine GitHub-committed multi-year Inside Airbnb archives appear to be rare — most repos re-download the CDN's current files on demand rather than committing historical CSVs, which matches the CONTEXT.md framing that CDN retention (~1yr) is the actual gap. The single best find is NOT an Inside-Airbnb mirror at all: Tom Slee's independent airbnb-data-collection project (2014-2017, dozens of cities) predates Inside Airbnb's own public data and is hosted off-GitHub (tomslee.net) — a human should verify that site is still live and pull the actual files before relying on it, since the code repo itself is unmaintained and the linked bulk-data host was not directly fetched (WebFetch would not follow off-domain host without a specific file URL). Did not find any GitHub Release assets or LFS-backed multi-city listings.csv.gz archives, nor any Wayback/archive.org-specific GitHub tooling for the Inside Airbnb site (searches for those specific terms returned only unrelated project mirrors of Airbnb's own OSS libraries, e.g. airbnb/javascript, airbnb/lottie-*, which are style-guide/animation libraries and irrelevant here). Also did not check GitHub Gists or Kaggle notebook 'code' tabs (out of scope for this modality). A logical next step for another scout/modality: check tomslee.net directly (WebFetch) and check Wayback Machine CDX for insideairbnb.com/*.csv.gz snapshots pre-2023 (a Wayback-focused modality, not gh search).
